Meta description: What HeyGen, Creatify, OpusClip, Synthesia, Arcads and the rest actually cost in 2026, plan by plan, next to Fastlane pricing. Read from each pricing page and dated.
Theme color: #ffffff
# What every AI content tool actually costs
Plan by plan, read from each vendor's own pricing page and dated, with the limits that decide what you really pay. Fastlane's own pricing is below for the comparison.
## Fastlane pricing
Plan | Price | Includes
Starter | $29 / month | 500 credits a month (up to 100 statics or 6 videos), Light planning from Senna, 1 campaign at a time, 1 social account, 1 seat, 25 AI characters, Trending content library, TikTok direct posting, unlimited scheduling
Growth | $79 / month | 2,000 credits a month (up to 400 statics or 25 videos), 4x the Senna fuel, 5 campaigns at a time, 10 social accounts per workspace, 3 workspaces, 3 seats included, $10 a month per extra, Analytics, remix and auto captions, Unlimited AI characters, 100 real-person characters, Priority support
Pro | $199 / month | 7,500 credits a month (up to 1,500 statics or 93 videos), 5x the Senna fuel, 20 campaigns at a time, 500 social accounts per workspace, 10 workspaces, 10 seats included, $10 a month per extra, Unlimited AI and real-person characters, Analytics, remix, auto captions, priority support
Enterprise | $999 / month | 40,000 credits a month (up to 8,000 statics or 500 videos), Every Pro feature, 14x the Senna fuel, 25 seats included, 20 campaigns at a time, 500 social accounts per workspace, 10 workspaces, Scales to $2,999 a month in $50 steps, each adds 2,000 credits
Warmed accounts | $100 / mo per account | Real TikTok or Instagram accounts created and warmed by humans in your niche, plus $1.50 per post upload
## Competitor pricing guides
Buffer pricing starts free (3 channels, 1 user, 10 scheduled posts per channel) and moves to $6 per channel per month on Essentials or $12 per channel per month on Team, with roughly 20% off on annual billing and volume discounts once you pass 10 channels.
Captions AI pricing starts at $24.99 per month for the Max plan with 500 AI credits, then the Frontier tiers (renamed from Scale) at $69.99 (1,400 credits), $139.99 (2,800) and $279.99 (5,600) per month, plus a custom Enterprise tier. The free plan is $0 but includes no AI credits, so auto-captions, AI twins and dubbing all need a paid plan.
Vizard AI pricing starts free (60 credits per month, 720p, one social account), then Creator at $29 per month or $14.50 per month billed annually ($174 a year), and Business at $39 per month or $19.50 annually ($234 a year), with Enterprise custom. Both paid plans start at 600 credits per month and the credit tier is selectable up to 74,400 credits per year.
Vidyo.ai (Quso.ai) pricing starts free with 75 credits per month, watermarked 720p exports and TikTok-only publishing, then Lite at $29 per month ($19 annually), Essential at $39 ($26 annually) and Growth at $49 ($33 annually), with credits doubling on annual billing. Multi-platform scheduling now starts on Essential; Lite publishes to TikTok only.
AutoShorts AI pricing starts at $19 per month or $16 per month billed yearly (Starter, up to 3 posts per week, 27 motion credits), then $39 or $33 yearly (Daily, one post a day, 62 motion credits) and $69 or $58 yearly (Hardcore, two posts a day, 124 motion credits). The free option was only ever a single video and is marked temporarily paused, and every plan allows one active video series.
2short AI pricing starts with a free plan of 30 minutes of AI video analysis per month, then Lite at $9.90 per month for 5 hours, Pro at $19.90 for 15 hours with unlimited exports, and Premium at $49.90 for 50 hours. No annual pricing is listed.
Superscale pricing starts at $49 per month (Starter: 4,000 credits), then Advanced at $99 (8,000 credits, up to 250 generations, 1 brand, 2 seats), Pro at $199 (16,000 credits, 5 brands, 5 seats), Scale at $399 (32,000 credits, 15 brands) and Enterprise from $799 per month. There is no free plan; new accounts get trial credits and a 5-day free trial.
HeyGen pricing starts free (3 watermarked videos per month, one minute each), then Creator at $29 per month or $24 billed annually for 600 credits, Pro from $49 per month for 1,000 credits with 4K export and Seedance 2.5 and Veo 3.1 access, Business at $149 per month plus $20 per seat for 1,500 credits, and Enterprise custom. The API is pay-as-you-go and priced separately. Unused credits roll over one extra month on monthly plans.
Synthesia pricing starts with a free Basic plan (500 credits per month plus a free allowance of 10 minutes of video or dubbing, watermarked), then Starter at $19 per month ($9 for the first month) or $14 per month billed annually for 1,250 credits, about 12 more minutes of video, and Pro, renamed from Creator, at $89 per month ($49 for the first month) or $59 annually for 6,000 credits, about 60 minutes. Pro scales to 48,000 credits a month at $676 ($329 annually), and Enterprise is custom with unlimited minutes.
OpusClip pricing starts with a free tier (60 credits per month, watermarked captions, no editing, exports expire after 3 days), then Starter at $15 per month for 150 credits, and Pro at $29 per month or $14.50 per month billed annually ($174 a year) for 300 credits per month that roll over for 2 months, 2 seats and 6 social connections, with on-demand top-ups and up to 15 packs per account. Business is custom.
InVideo pricing is per seat and the plans were renamed and repriced: Starter at $20 per seat per month or $10 billed annually (400 credits), Plus at $60 or $30 billed annually (2,000 credits, with a 5,000-credit option), and Max at $250 per seat per month, the same monthly or annually (8,000 credits, with 10,000 and 15,000 options). Business plans start at $79 per seat for Team (1,600 credits per seat, 5 to 30 seats) and $215 per seat for Scale, with Enterprise on request. A free plan exists but is only shown after signup, with limited weekly-resetting credits.
Blaze AI pricing starts at $79 per month for Starter (3 posting accounts, 600 credits, 1 user), then Growth at $149 per month (10 accounts, 1,500 credits, unlimited users) and All-In-One at $999 per month for a fully managed funnel. There is no free plan; Starter and Growth offer a 7-day trial with no credit card.
Creatify pricing starts free (10 credits per month, up to 2 video ads or 20 image ads, 300 AI actors, watermarked), then Standard at $15 per month for 55 credits, Pro at $55 per month for 280 credits with the Ad Agent, Ad Clone and competitor tracker, Max at $95 per month for 730 credits and 3 seats, and Business at $195 per month for 1,500 credits and 10 seats. Annual billing saves 30% ($10, $38, $66 and $136 per month), and Enterprise is custom.
Arcads still does not publish pricing; its /pricing URL returned a 404 again on 1 November 2026 and plans are shown only after signup. Third-party breakdowns based on in-app screenshots report Starter at about $110 per month for 10 videos, Creator at about $220 per month for 20 videos, and a custom Pro tier with cloned actors, team features and API access. There is no free plan, but the homepage now says a free trial is available, without stating its length or limits.
MakeUGC pricing shows Starter at $59 per month for 500 credits, Growth at $79 for 1,000 credits and Pro from $149 for 2,000 to 5,000 credits. Billed annually, those drop to $29, $39 and $79 per month (the page labels this a 51% and 47% saving), and quarterly billing sits in between at $41, $55 and $104. API and MCP access are now included on every plan and draw on the same credits, with volume API pricing on the custom Enterprise tier. There is no free plan; a $1 trial is offered and renews at the plan price.
ReelFarm pricing starts at $49 per month for Growth (100 slideshows, 10 formats), then Scale at $95 per month (250 slideshows, 20 formats) and Enterprise at $195 per month (750 slideshows, 200 formats, bring your own Anthropic key for unlimited generation). Every tier includes native TikTok publishing, scheduling, unlimited connected TikTok accounts and unlimited team members. The site advertises three free TikToks to start.

### Paste your Shop listing

# How to Make Product Demo Videos That Actually Work (for Fastlane Uploads)
Your hook stops the scroll — your demo turns attention into interest. Here’s how to film short, natural demos that make people feel like they discovered your app.
Your hook might stop the scroll, but your product demo is what turns attention into interest. It’s where viewers go from “cool idea” to “wait, that’s actually useful.” But most people overthink it, they make their demo sound like a pitch deck.
For organic content, your demo should feel like a friend showing you something clever, not a founder explaining a roadmap. Think 90% story or curiosity, 10% product.
The goal is to make people feel like they discovered your app.
## What Makes a Great Demo
Good demos are quick, natural, and visually clean.
They show real usage, not perfect performances.
Natural gestures, real data, genuine reactions, even small “oops” moments make it feel human.
Your job is to capture the core moment when someone gets the value.
If someone can watch your video and instantly understand what your product does and why it’s cool, you’ve done it right.
## 1. iOS Screen Recording Demos
### Setup
- Use the built-in iOS screen recorder (Control Center → Screen Recording)
- Record in portrait (9:16) for TikTok, Reels, Shorts (usually, you configure this later, inside an editor like CapCut)
- Turn on Do Not Disturb
- Close all background apps
- Turn off HDR mode in camera settings (it can cause strange screen brightness shifts in your footage)
### Recording
- Start recording before opening your app
- Open the app with one smooth swipe
- Show your main feature flow — the part real users actually use
- Keep it under 15 seconds
- End on your strongest visual payoff
### Pro Tips
- Record your real hand or gestures when possible — adds authenticity
- Do multiple takes and keep the cleanest one
- Use real data, not placeholder text
- One clear action per clip
## 2. Web App Demos (Laptop Recording)
- Record with your phone in portrait mode
- Frame the laptop screen so it fills most of the shot
- Use natural light or a soft ring light
- Keep your phone stable (tripod or stacked books)
### Preparation
- Close tabs and clean your desktop
- Use incognito mode for a minimal browser
- Zoom browser to 125–150% for clarity
- Angle your laptop slightly for a better view
- Show natural hand use on the keyboard or trackpad
- Keep cursor movements deliberate and slow
- Pause briefly on key screens
- Show your face or hands reacting if it feels natural
### Highlight
- Capture the “input → output” flow
- Focus on your product’s aha moment
- Show real results or data
## Optional: Add Text Overlay or Feature Highlights
While raw demos can work perfectly on their own, sometimes adding light text overlays makes the value clearer, especially when showing multiple features in one clip.
You can experiment by:
- Stitching together short clips that each show one feature
- Adding small text labels to each section (e.g. “Replies to Reddit leads” → then cut to a Reddit clip “Makes viral TikTok slideshows too” → then show the slideshow builder)
- Keeping text subtle and natural, not salesy or intrusive
This works best if you’re editing in CapCut, iMovie, or any quick video editor.
The key is testing: try both clean demos and text-highlight versions, then see which performs better. Fastlane helps you upload and track both.
## Universal Demo Rules
### Timing
- 10–15 seconds max
- One key action per clip
- End on your money shot
### Content
- Show the problem being solved
- Real use, real context
- Make it feel effortless
### Quality
- Bright, stable footage
- Clear visuals
- Good lighting on screens
- Clean, crisp audio if there’s voice
### Editing
- Trim hesitation
- Speed up loading screens
- Subtle zooms on key actions
- Clean, quick transitions
### Avoid These
- Long walkthroughs
- Fake or placeholder data
- Over-explaining obvious things
- Shaky handheld footage
- Videos longer than 15 seconds
## How to Tell You Nailed It
A great demo sparks organic curiosity:
- Comments like “What app is this?”
- Saves, shares, profile visits
- Users tagging friends or replying with “need this”
## Aftermark Upload Tip
Before you upload to Fastlane, double-check that:
- It’s short (under 15s)
- HDR is off
- Natural lighting is on
- Real data is used
- Optional text overlays highlight key moments if helpful

Meta description: Wan 3.0 explained for short-form marketers: Alibaba's AI video model, launched 24 August 2026, generates up to 30 second clips at up to 1080p with audio in the same pass, turns documents and web pages into video, and costs $0.05 to $0.20 per second.
Theme color: #ffffff
# Wan 3.0: Alibaba's 30 second AI video model, explained
Wan 3.0 is the newest model in Alibaba's Wan video family. It doubles the clip ceiling to 30 seconds, generates sound with the picture, and does something no other mainstream video model leads with: it builds a video from a PDF, a slide deck, a spreadsheet or a web page. Here is what that means for a TikTok, Reels and Shorts calendar.
Wan 3.0 is Alibaba Cloud's AI video generation model, released in public beta on 6 August 2026 and officially launched on 24 August 2026: it generates clips of up to 30 seconds in a single pass at 480p, 720p or 1080p with audio generated in the same pass, accepts text, images, audio, video, documents and web pages as input, and costs $0.05, $0.10 or $0.20 per output second by resolution. Unlike Wan 2.1 and 2.2, its weights are closed.
For marketers the headline is length plus inputs: a full 30 second ad in one generation, built from material you already have, such as a product page or a pitch deck.
## Wan 3.0 specs
Maker | Alibaba Cloud
Released | Public beta from 6 August 2026 (application based); official launch 24 August 2026
Max clip length | Up to 30 seconds in one generation, double the 15 second ceiling of Wan 2.7
Resolution | 480p, 720p and 1080p. No 4K tier
Native audio | Yes: audio generated in the same pass as the video, with multilingual voice output
Inputs | Text, images, audio and video references, plus documents (PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Markdown and Apple iWork formats) and web page URLs
Pricing | Alibaba Cloud list price in Singapore: $0.05 per second at 480p, $0.10 at 720p and $0.20 at 1080p (about $12 per minute at 1080p); about $0.041, $0.083 and $0.165 per second in the Beijing, Tokyo, Frankfurt, Virginia and Hong Kong regions. A faster wan3.0-video-prime variant lists at $0.068, $0.14 and $0.28 per second in Singapore
Weights | Closed, API only. The last open-weight Wan release is Wan 2.2 (Apache 2.0)
Access | Alibaba Cloud Model Studio and Qwen Cloud (model ID wan3.0-video); consumer access on wan.video rolling out to members
Benchmark | Not verified: no independent benchmark results had been published at launch
## What changed in Wan 3.0
Wan 2.1 and 2.2 were open-weight; Wan 2.5, 2.6 and 2.7 moved to closed commercial APIs. Wan 2.7 (April 2026) added a Thinking Mode, first and last frame control and instruction-based editing, with clips up to 15 seconds. Wan 3.0 doubles the ceiling to 30 seconds per generation, generates audio with the picture, and adds document and web page inputs so a deck, spreadsheet or product page can be turned into a video that follows its structure. Alibaba says instruction following, shot-to-shot consistency and audio quality all improved, though no independent benchmarks back that up yet.
## How to get Wan 3.0
Alibaba Cloud Model Studio and Qwen Cloud APIs, billed per second of output by resolution. Consumer access through wan.video is rolling out to members, and third-party platforms such as Morphic also offer it. No self-hosting.
## What Wan 3.0 means for short-form marketers
Thirty seconds changes what one generation can be. Most AI video models stop at 8 to 15 seconds, so a full hook, demo and call to action has meant stitching clips together. Wan 3.0 can produce the whole beat in one pass, which keeps a character, a product and a voice consistent across the entire ad.
Document and web page inputs are the genuinely new idea. Marketing teams already own the source material: a product page, a launch deck, a feature spreadsheet. Being able to hand that to the model and get a structured video back is a fast way to draft explainers and product walkthroughs, though Alibaba itself flags on-screen text accuracy as an area still improving, so check every caption.
At $0.20 per second, a 30 second 1080p clip costs about $6, and 720p halves that. Feeds compress hard, so test at 720p first, and remember that long single shots without a story turn tend to feel slow on TikTok: the hook still has to land in the first two seconds.
## Where Wan 3.0 still needs care
- Closed weights: no self-hosting or fine-tuning, unlike Wan 2.1 and 2.2
- Tops out at 1080p, with no 4K tier
- Alibaba acknowledges audio texture and on-screen text accuracy still need work
